tagline: A Mekong border town with the Friendship Bridge to Laos, Sala Kaew Ku, and the Naga fireballs
introHtml: Nong Khai is a small town on the Mekong, right on the border with Laos, looking across to Vientiane on the far bank. Most visitors spend the late afternoon strolling along the river, catching the breeze at the Naga Plaza and the walking street, then drop by Tha Sadet Market for snacks and gifts brought over from Laos. In town, Wat Pho Chai houses Luang Pho Phra Sai, the city's most revered Buddha image, and Sala Kaew Ku is packed with giant, oddly captivating concrete sculptures. Come the end of Buddhist Lent, people from across the region gather to watch the Naga fireballs rise from the river. Nong Khai is an easy place to wander — riverside, temples, markets — and it's also the gateway across the Friendship Bridge into Laos for a day trip.
bestTime: October–February, when it's cool and pleasant for walking along the Mekong; the end of Buddhist Lent in October brings the Naga fireball festival

highlights.name: The Mekong riverfront and Naga Plaza
highlights.blurb: A walkway along the Mekong in the middle of town where people come out for the evening breeze and a view across to Laos. The Naga Plaza is a popular photo spot, and there's a walking street on weekends.

highlights.name: Sala Kaew Ku
highlights.blurb: A sculpture park of huge concrete figures built on the faith of Pu Bunleua — a seven-headed naga, Buddha images, and giant statues with hidden moral meanings. You can easily spend an hour walking through it.

highlights.name: Luang Pho Phra Sai, Wat Pho Chai
highlights.blurb: Nong Khai's most revered Buddha image, held dear across the whole province. People come to pay respects non-stop, and it's usually the first stop for anyone visiting the town.

highlights.name: Tha Sadet Market
highlights.blurb: A riverside market selling gifts, snacks, and goods from Laos and Vietnam — mu yo, naem, woven textiles, and dried foods. An enjoyable place to shop for things to take home.

highlights.name: Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
highlights.blurb: The first bridge across the Mekong, linking Nong Khai with Vientiane. People use it to cross into Laos on a morning-out-evening-back day trip, and it's the starting point for trips over the border.

highlights.name: Naga fireballs
highlights.blurb: A phenomenon of pinkish-orange fireballs rising from the Mekong around the end of Buddhist Lent. People from across the region and visitors gather along the river near Phon Phisai and Rattanawapi districts to watch.

foodScene.name: Vietnamese food
foodScene.note: Naem nueang, mu yo, and fresh spring rolls turn up all over town thanks to the Vietnamese communities along the Mekong — they're a Nong Khai specialty.

foodScene.name: Mekong river fish
foodScene.note: Riverside spots cook freshwater fish every way — grilled, tom yum, larb pla, and pla khang. Sit and eat in the cool breeze with a view of the Laos side.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and bold-flavored bamboo-shoot soup are everyday meals for Nong Khai folks, just like the rest of the region. You'll find them in every corner of town.

foodScene.name: Kuay jap yuan and khao piak sen
foodScene.note: Soft Vietnamese-style rice noodles in a clear broth with a sprinkle of pepper — a popular breakfast that comes from the Vietnamese communities along the river.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and grilled meats
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) places are scattered all over town, a go-to dinner for groups, especially along the main road and near the river.

foodScene.name: Riverside cafes
foodScene.note: There are several cafes and coffee shops with Mekong views — sip a coffee looking over to Laos in the morning, or take a break before heading out to the market.

foodScene.name: Gifts from Laos and Vietnam
foodScene.note: Mu yo, naem, Isan sausage, and dried goods from Tha Sadet Market — easy to buy as gifts at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Walking street street food
foodScene.note: The riverside walking street on weekends has grilled and fried snacks and local sweets to nibble on in the evening, with the river right there.

attractions.name: Mekong riverside walkway and Naga Plaza
attractions.blurb: A walkway along the Mekong in the middle of town, with the Naga Plaza as a photo spot. People come out for the breeze and an evening stroll, looking across to Laos.

attractions.name: Sala Kaew Ku
attractions.blurb: A large sculpture park with a seven-headed naga, Buddha images, and statues carrying hidden moral meanings. You can walk the whole garden taking in the unusual concrete work.

attractions.name: Wat Pho Chai
attractions.blurb: The temple that houses Luang Pho Phra Sai, Nong Khai's most revered Buddha image. People from across the province come to pay respects non-stop — an important temple in the heart of town.

attractions.name: Tha Sadet Market
attractions.blurb: A riverside market selling gifts, snacks, and goods from Laos and Vietnam — mu yo, naem, woven textiles, and dried foods. An enjoyable place to shop.

attractions.name: Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
attractions.blurb: The bridge across the Mekong linking Nong Khai with Vientiane — the crossing point for a morning-out-evening-back day trip into Laos.

attractions.name: Wat Pha Tak Suea
attractions.blurb: A hilltop temple with a glass-floored skywalk jutting out over the valley, with views of the winding Mekong and the Laos side stretching into the distance.

attractions.name: Phon Phisai District
attractions.blurb: A stretch of the Mekong that's a prime spot for watching the Naga fireballs around the end of Buddhist Lent. Off-season it's a quiet riverside town good for a stroll and some Mekong fish.

attractions.name: Wat Hin Mak Peng
attractions.blurb: A riverside meditation retreat shaded by forest and large boulders. The calm atmosphere makes it a good place to walk around and unwind by the river.
